notes.title: One last feature before PSB will leave the Early Access
notes.notes:
Hi there.

By multiple requests from our users (and kids :) ) we feel compelled to add one last feature.

[h1]Settings dialog[/h1]

This dialog will allow parents to enable some useful browser features disabled by default (for the safest possible experience). 
 - Printer access
 - Allowing popups
 - Allowing mouse right button

Have any other similar limitations in mind? Do not hesitate to share.

Cheers,
Panda School Team.

notes.title: Update 2 is out! Now you can start the browser directly in the «Kids Mode».
notes.notes:
Yes, finally we have delivered the promised feature. You can now run the browser directly in the «Kids Mode» and when you exit the app you will get back to your desktop at once. Pretty convenient. 

The only problem... is the way Steam works with shortcuts :(

This new «Kids Mode» launch can be easily triggered from "Library" section of Steam App. Just click "Launch" when our app is selected and you'll see small dialog with a choice between regular and kid modes.

Same small dialog is triggered when you right-click on the steam icon in your tray bar and select "Panda School Browser" from the list of recent apps.

Of course we realize, that it is not the perfect way to run a browser.
So we suggest the following steps to manually create a «Kids Mode» shortcut on your desktop:

[olist]
[*] Right click on the Panda School Browser in your Steam App -> Library -> Software section and select "Properties".
[*] Click on the "Local Files" tab.
[*] Click on the "Browse Local Files..." button
[*] Drag the "PandaSchoolBrowser.exe" file (the one with the panda face on it) with your RIGHT mouse button to your desktop. When releasing a button you'll see a contextual menu and should select "Create shortcuts here". 
Attention - if you will use the left mouse button you'll just copy the exe file to your desktop, and it will not work as a shortcut.
[*] Right click on the shortcut and select "Properties".
[*] Add the argument --direct-child-mode to the "Target" input. It should be added AFTER the closing double-quote.
[/olist]

Final result should look similar to 
[code]
"F:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Panda School Browser\PandaSchoolBrowser.exe" --direct-child-mode
[/code]

Sorry for the compicated setup... but unfortunately Steam does not allow more useful alternatives. If you happen to find a better way to handle this - let us know, please.

notes.title: "Roadmap" for the next few months
notes.notes:
Here is the promised "Roadmap" update or "How exactly are we planning to improve our browser".

[h1]Update 2 (approximate delivery - mid-August):[/h1]
Starting the browser directly in the kids mode. Exit from the kids mode to desktop. We will also investigate auto-start possibility for the browser and hope to make it by the date too. But it is not a guarantee, since there are quite many tricks to take into account.

[h1]Update 3 (approximate delivery - mid-September):[/h1]
"Classroom Folders" feature. Graphical prototype can be found here: http://pandaschool.org/img/misc/panda_school_folders_prototype.jpg

People who are interested in beta-testing the features (and may be affecting the outcome :) ) are welcome. Leave comments here or write us directly: info@pandaschool.org.

Cheers

notes.title: "Private Classes" feature is ready!
notes.notes:
"Private classes" feature is finally available for everyone.
Shortly - parents now able to add any number of their own (private) classes to their "Classroom", without any moderation from our side.

Here is a small screenshot explaining the outcome:
http://pandaschool.org/img/misc/panda-private-class.png

Orange "ball" at the bottom-right corner of your class is an indicator of a private one. All classes added to your "Classroom" are available for your child in "Kids Mode".

[b][IMPORTANT] You should reload your "Classroom" once (press the "home" button or click on the "Classroom" tab) for private class to become available after adding it. Otherwise your class will be blocked and "Stop" sign will appear when trying to navigate on it.[/b]

Enjoy! But also be responsible, remember that there are plenty of websites on the internet not ready for smaller kids and providing poor unwanted experience.

[b]"With great power comes great responsibility"[/b]
